source.citation: Powers, T. C. (1948). A discussion of cement hydration in relation to the curing of concrete. Proceedings of the Highway Research Board 27, 178-188.

transcription.from: src/kinetics/rate_models.jl (the two ratios) and docs/src/tutorials/self_desiccation.md (the split of the sealed ratio), ChemistryLab 0.22.1
transcription.note: Moved out of the code unchanged. The proceedings have no DOI and the article was not re-read during the move; the values are the ones the package has used and documented since it first cited this source.

w_c_sealed.description: Water/cement ratio below which a sealed paste cannot hydrate completely: non-evaporable water plus gel water.

w_c_saturated.description: The same bound when curing water is supplied from outside, the chemical shrinkage being refilled.

non_evaporable_water.description: Non-evaporable water per gram of cement at complete hydration, g/g: the water that survives D-drying, part of the sealed ratio.

gel_water.description: Gel water per gram of cement at complete hydration, g/g: the rest of the sealed ratio.

notes: The difference between the two ratios, 0.06 g of water per gram of cement, is the chemical shrinkage.
